facts.value: A replication crisis in psychology has emerged, with many notable findings not being replicated, leading to accusations of fraudulent results.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: As many as two-thirds of highly publicized findings in psychology failed to be replicated.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Reproducibility has generally been stronger in cognitive psychology than in social psychology and subfields of differential psychology.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Other implicated subfields in the replication crisis include clinical psychology, developmental psychology, and educational research.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: The focus on the replication crisis has led to renewed efforts in the discipline to retest important findings.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: 295 psychology and medical journals have adopted result-blind peer review where studies are accepted based on methodological rigor prior to data collection.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Large-scale collaborations among researchers working in multiple labs in different countries have taken place, with collaborators making their data openly available.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Allen and Mehler estimated that 61 percent of result-blind studies have yielded null results, in contrast to an estimated 5 to 20 percent in traditional research.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick
